definitions.explanation: A flavorful liquid base used in Japanese cooking, typically made from kombu (kelp), katsuobushi (dried bonito flakes), or both.

examples.notes: 出汁を取る is the standard expression for making/extracting dashi

examples.japanese: ⟦{昆布|こんぶ}→昆布：04934_konbu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{鰹節|かつおぶし}→鰹節：04935_katsuobushi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{出汁|だし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}りました→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: I made dashi from kelp and dried bonito flakes.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{味噌汁|みそしる}→味噌汁：04954_misoshiru⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{出汁|だし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{効|き}いていて→効く：01932_kiku⟧⟦{美味|おい}しい→美味しい：00740_oishii⟧。
examples.english: This miso soup tastes good because the dashi flavor comes through well.
examples.notes: 出汁が効く means the dashi flavor is prominent

notes:
{出汁|だし} is the foundational flavoring liquid in Japanese cooking, essential to ⟦{味噌汁|みそしる}→味噌汁：04954_misoshiru⟧, ⟦{煮物|にもの}→煮物：04971_nimono⟧, and many other dishes. It provides the umami base that defines Japanese cuisine.

TYPES:
- ⟦{昆布|こんぶ}→昆布：04934_konbu⟧{出汁|だし}: kelp stock
- ⟦{鰹|かつお}→鰹：06106_katsuo⟧{出汁|だし}: bonito stock
- ⟦{合|あ}わせ→合わせる：01872_awaseru⟧{出汁|だし}: combination stock (kelp + bonito)
- ⟦{煮干|にぼ}し→煮干し：13408_niboshi⟧{出汁|だし}: dried sardine stock

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {出汁|だし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧: to make/extract stock
- {出汁|だし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{効|き}いている→効く：01932_kiku⟧: the dashi flavor comes through well
- ⟦{顆粒|かりゅう}→顆粒：24069_karyuu⟧だし: instant dashi granules

WRITING:
Also written as だし or ダシ in casual contexts. The kanji {出汁|だし} is an ⟦{当|あ}て{字|じ}→当て字：12539_ateji⟧ (kanji applied for phonetic value).

CULTURAL NOTE:
Making dashi from scratch is considered a key skill in Japanese cooking, though instant granules are widely used for everyday meals.
